standard: Structured Clinical Dosing, KDIGO Renal, Pregnancy/LactMed, LiverTox, CredibleMeds QT & AGS Beers Reference

ibuprofen.typical_range: 200-400 mg every 6-8 hours (max 1200 mg/day OTC; up to 2400 mg/day prescription)
ibuprofen.renal_note: KDIGO: Avoid NSAIDs if eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2; avoid prolonged use if eGFR 30-59 due to acute kidney injury risk.
ibuprofen.pregnancy_note: Contraindicated in 3rd trimester (premature closure of fetal ductus arteriosus and oligohydramnios); avoid after 20 weeks gestation.
ibuprofen.lactmed_status: Preferred NSAID in breastfeeding (extremely low milk levels)
ibuprofen.beers_note: AGS Beers: Avoid chronic use in adults >=65 years due to high risk of peptic ulcer disease, GI bleeding, and AKI.

diclofenac.renal_note: KDIGO: Contraindicated in severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min); high nephrotoxicity risk.
diclofenac.pregnancy_note: Contraindicated in 3rd trimester of pregnancy (ductus arteriosus closure).
diclofenac.lactmed_status: Low milk levels; ibuprofen preferred in lactation
diclofenac.beers_note: AGS Beers: Avoid in older adults (>=65 years) due to GI bleeding, renal injury, and elevated cardiovascular thrombotic risk.

naproxen.renal_note: KDIGO: Not recommended if eGFR < 30 mL/min.
naproxen.lactmed_status: Avoid in breastfeeding due to long half-life; use ibuprofen instead
naproxen.beers_note: AGS Beers: Avoid chronic use in adults >=65 years due to GI bleed risk.

celecoxib.renal_note: Avoid in severe renal insufficiency (eGFR < 30 mL/min).
celecoxib.beers_note: AGS Beers: Caution in older adults with cardiovascular, renal, or GI risk.

mefenamic acid.renal_note: Contraindicated in preexisting renal disease or eGFR < 30 mL/min.
mefenamic acid.lactmed_status: Ibuprofen preferred over mefenamic acid during lactation
mefenamic acid.beers_note: AGS Beers: Avoid in older adults (>=65 years) due to GI and renal toxicity.

aspirin.typical_range: Antiplatelet: 75-150 mg once daily; Analgesic: 300-600 mg q4-6h
aspirin.renal_note: Low-dose antiplatelet (75-100 mg) safe in CKD; avoid high analgesic doses (>325 mg) if eGFR < 30.
aspirin.pregnancy_note: Low-dose aspirin (75-150 mg) used for preeclampsia prophylaxis; avoid high analgesic doses in 3rd trimester.
aspirin.lactmed_status: Low-dose (75-100 mg) acceptable; avoid high analgesic doses in breastfeeding (Reye syndrome risk)
aspirin.beers_note: AGS Beers: Avoid aspirin >325 mg/day in older adults; do not initiate low-dose aspirin for primary prevention in adults >=70 years.

warfarin.typical_range: 2-10 mg once daily titrated to INR
warfarin.renal_note: Close INR monitoring required in severe CKD (eGFR < 30) due to higher bleeding risk.
warfarin.pregnancy_note: CONTRAINDICATED IN PREGNANCY (Fetal warfarin syndrome / teratogenicity and fetal hemorrhage; switch to LMWH).
warfarin.lactmed_status: Compatible with breastfeeding (not excreted in breast milk in measurable amounts)

clopidogrel.typical_range: 75 mg once daily (up to 300-600 mg single loading dose in ACS)

amoxicillin.renal_note: KDIGO: If eGFR 10-30 mL/min, limit to 250-500 mg every 12 hours; if eGFR < 10, 250-500 mg every 24 hours.
amoxicillin.livertox_class: Category B (Rare idiosyncratic; higher with clavulanate)

clavulanate.renal_note: KDIGO: Do not use 875/125 mg or 1000 mg tablet if eGFR < 30 mL/min; adjust interval to q12h.
clavulanate.livertox_class: Category A (Leading antibiotic cause of cholestatic DILI)

azithromycin.typical_range: 500 mg once daily (or 500 mg day 1 then 250 mg days 2-5)

clarithromycin.renal_note: KDIGO: Reduce clarithromycin dose by 50% if eGFR < 30 mL/min.

ciprofloxacin.renal_note: KDIGO: If eGFR < 30 mL/min, reduce dose to 250-500 mg every 18-24 hours.
ciprofloxacin.pregnancy_note: Avoid fluoroquinolones in pregnancy unless no safer alternative exists (fetal cartilage toxicity risk).
ciprofloxacin.lactmed_status: Acceptable short-term; monitor infant for diarrhea
ciprofloxacin.beers_note: AGS Beers: Increased risk of tendinitis/tendon rupture, CNS toxicity, and aortic aneurysm in older adults.

metronidazole.lactmed_status: Compatible; high single 2g dose may warrant 12-24h interruption

metformin.renal_note: KDIGO: CONTRAINDICATED if eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2 (lactic acidosis risk). If eGFR 30-44 mL/min, do not initiate or reduce maintenance dose to max 1000 mg/day.
metformin.lactmed_status: Compatible with breastfeeding (very low milk transfer)
metformin.livertox_class: Category D (Not hepatotoxic, but contraindicated in hepatic failure due to lactic acidosis)

gliclazide.typical_range: 40-160 mg twice daily (or 30-120 mg MR once daily)
gliclazide.renal_note: High risk of prolonged severe hypoglycemia in CKD Stage 4/5 (eGFR < 30 mL/min).
gliclazide.pregnancy_note: Avoid oral sulfonylureas in pregnancy; switch to insulin.
gliclazide.beers_note: AGS Beers: Sulfonylureas carry higher risk of severe prolonged hypoglycemia in older adults.

enalapril.renal_note: KDIGO: Start at 2.5 mg daily if eGFR < 30 mL/min and monitor serum creatinine and potassium within 1-2 weeks.
enalapril.pregnancy_note: BOXED WARNING / CONTRAINDICATED IN PREGNANCY (Fetal renal dysplasia, oligohydramnios, skull hypoplasia, and fetal death).
enalapril.lactmed_status: Compatible with breastfeeding of full-term infants

lisinopril.renal_note: KDIGO: Reduce initial dose to 2.5-5 mg once daily if eGFR < 30 mL/min; monitor potassium and creatinine.
lisinopril.pregnancy_note: BOXED WARNING / CONTRAINDICATED IN PREGNANCY (Fetotoxic in 2nd and 3rd trimesters; discontinue immediately).
lisinopril.lactmed_status: Enalapril or captopril preferred during breastfeeding

losartan.renal_note: Monitor potassium and serum creatinine in CKD.
losartan.pregnancy_note: BOXED WARNING / CONTRAINDICATED IN PREGNANCY (Fetal renal failure, oligohydramnios, and death).
losartan.lactmed_status: Avoid in early lactation; enalapril or nifedipine preferred

spironolactone.typical_range: 25-50 mg once daily (up to 100-400 mg/day in cirrhosis)
spironolactone.renal_note: KDIGO: Avoid spironolactone if eGFR < 30 mL/min due to high risk of life-threatening hyperkalemia.
spironolactone.pregnancy_note: Avoid in pregnancy (anti-androgenic feminization of male fetus).
spironolactone.beers_note: AGS Beers: Avoid >25 mg/day in older adults with heart failure or CrCl < 30 mL/min due to hyperkalemia.

furosemide.lactmed_status: May suppress lactation at high doses

atorvastatin.pregnancy_note: Contraindicated in pregnancy (discontinue when pregnancy is recognized).
atorvastatin.livertox_class: Category A (Contraindicated in active liver disease / decompensated cirrhosis)

simvastatin.typical_range: 10-40 mg once daily in the evening
simvastatin.livertox_class: Category A (Contraindicated in active liver disease)

omeprazole.beers_note: AGS Beers: Avoid scheduled PPI use >8 weeks in older adults unless high-risk (e.g. chronic NSAIDs, Barrett's) due to C. difficile and bone loss risk.

pantoprazole.beers_note: AGS Beers: Review necessity if prescribed >8 weeks in adults >=65 years.

tramadol.renal_note: KDIGO: If eGFR < 30 mL/min, extend dosing interval to every 12 hours and do not exceed 200 mg/day.
tramadol.lactmed_status: FDA Warning: Avoid tramadol during breastfeeding (ultra-rapid CYP2D6 metabolizers risk infant respiratory depression)
tramadol.beers_note: AGS Beers: Max 300 mg/day in adults >75 years; causes CNS depression, falls, and SIADH/hyponatremia.

diazepam.pregnancy_note: Avoid chronic benzodiazepine use in pregnancy (neonatal withdrawal and floppy infant syndrome).
diazepam.lactmed_status: Avoid repeated doses during breastfeeding (long half-life causes infant sedation)
diazepam.beers_note: AGS Beers: Strongly avoid benzodiazepines in adults >=65 years due to cognitive impairment, delirium, falls, and fractures.

amitriptyline.typical_range: 10-75 mg at night (up to 150 mg/day in depression)
amitriptyline.lactmed_status: Low levels in milk; monitor infant for sedation
amitriptyline.beers_note: AGS Beers: Strongly avoid in adults >=65 years due to highly anticholinergic, sedating, and orthostatic hypotension effects.
